# Nexus

> Connect your agents once. Link your services once.

Nexus sits between AI coding agents and the services they use. It works out which
project an agent is in and sends each call to that project's own account and resource,
so an agent working on one project can't reach another project's services. Made for one
developer running several agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) across several projects.
Status: early build, Linux first.

## How it works

Agent → Project → Account → Resource

1. The agent asks Nexus for a service. It doesn't choose the project or the keys.
2. Nexus finds the project, then the account and resource linked to it. If it can't tell,
   or the project isn't registered, it refuses before any call is made.
3. Nexus makes the call with that account's login. The agent never sees the key.

Same service in a different project means a different account. Production and
development are kept apart too.

## What is covered

- About 50 popular services to start (list still under review).
- Built-in, reviewed support for Supabase and GitHub. Other services connect through their
  own MCP server and are protected at the account level, not the resource level, so use
  one account per project for those.
- Each project keeps a secret-free `.nexus/project.json`. Logins stay in the computer's
  secure storage.
- All agents connect to one local Nexus over HTTP. Claude Code and OpenCode report their
  folder to Nexus. Codex doesn't, so its folder is pinned in config. If an agent reports
  nothing, Nexus refuses.
- A live map of agents, projects and service accounts, plus a simple local activity log.

## What it is not

- Not a password manager, a company governance tool, or a file sandbox.
- It can't see or stop anything an agent does without going through Nexus.
- Guard (reviewing risky actions) may come later. It is not built.

## Pricing (proposal, not final)

Free: up to 2 projects. Pro: about $10–12 a month or $99 a year. Team/Agency: later.
The core stays free.
